title: syg check --format json
description: What `syg check` and `syg build` write with --format json (CLI-Check-001, DIAG-001): one object, naming this schema as its $schema, with the findings in the order the text format prints them. Fields are added, never renamed or removed, within a major version (docs/compatibility.md).

$schema.description: This schema's URL, so that an editor or a validator finds it.

findings.description: Every finding, error, warning and note, in the order the text format prints them.

severity.description: error fails the command (exit 1); warning fails it under --strict; info never does (CHK-Sev-001).

code.description: A rule ID (CHK-…), or a compiler phase for a finding that is not a rule (syntax, resolve, type, …). `syg explain CODE` documents every one.

name.description: The rule's readable name (budget-blocks-eviction), which `syg explain` and syg.yaml accept beside the code. Absent for a finding that is not a rule's.

position.description: The primary span. A finding about the module as a whole has an empty file and zero positions.

secondary.description: Related spans, each with what it contributes (DIAG-003).

consequence.description: What fails in production, and how (DIAG-004).

suggestion.description: The computable fix, when there is one (DIAG-005).

explain.description: The `syg explain` topic for this finding.

environment.description: The environment the finding is in; absent for the base module.

snapshot.description: For a Tier-2 finding, the snapshot it was checked against.

file.description: As the module was named on the command line; empty when the finding has no location.
